references.text: The same ritual act of smearing blood on the horns of the altar and pouring out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar is described for the sin offering for a priest.
An identical procedure with the blood on the horns of the altar and pouring it out at the base is described for the sin offering for the whole congregation of Israel.
The same blood ritual is performed by the priest with his finger on the burnt offering altar for the sin offering of a leader.
A parallel action where the priest takes blood with his finger and smears it on the horns of the burnt offering altar for the sin offering of a goat.
Moses performs the same blood ritual at the consecration of Aaron and his sons, with blood on the horns of the altar and at its base.
Aaron performs the blood ritual with his finger on the horns of the altar and pours out the blood at the base of the altar on the eighth day.
Instructions to take blood, smear it on the horns of the altar, and pour out the rest at the base of the altar are given in connection with the consecration of the altar.
The Letter to the Hebrews explains that almost everything is cleansed with blood according to the law, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.
